Premier Capitaine de la Death Guard, La: First Captain of the Death Guard, the Left Hand of Mortarion, Master of the Terminus Est. The First Captain of the Death Guard Legion was once part of the Legion's Librarius, but owing to his Primarch Mortarion's distrust of psykers, Typhon suppressed his gifts and strove to develop his talents as a war leader. His strength, skill and bearing saw him rise through the ranks until he found himself in command of the starship Terminus Est and the alchemical arsenal it held. Although he had renounced his role as a psyker, the Warp continued to exert its influence on Typhon, for he was one of the first to succumb to the insidious whispers of the dark powers.
Premier Capitaine des Blood Angels, L'Ar: First Captain of the Blood Angels, The Archein of Wisdom, The Tranquil Angel.
Premier Capitaine des Night Lords, Le Pr: First Captain of the Night Lords, the Prince of Crows, and Master of the Atramentar. Jago Sevatarion has the grim honour of being the first Traitor ever to have cried "Death to the false Emperor". As gifted as he is arrogant, Sevatar is a cruel fighter, impervious to the concept of honour. This attitude is reflected in his appearance, carefully studied to inspire fear. His midnight-blue armour is adorned with flayed skins and his helm is sculpted into a grinning skull. This morbid visage hides not only the soul of a murderer, but also a gift of latent psychic powers which, though he suppresses them, allow Sevatar to enhance his abilities as a fighter still further.
Premier Capitaine des Sons of Horus, Gra: First Captain of the Sons of Horus, High Marshal of the Justaerin. Ezekyle Abaddon was a peerless warrior and the commander of the Justaerin Terminators. Similar in many ways to his Primarch, he shared with Horus in particular a savagery in battle and an innate tactical sense that earned him almost as many victories as his Primarch. Once regarded as a hero of the Imperium, Abaddon was devoted above all to Horus, and willingly followed him down the path of damnation.
Premier Capitaine des Word Bearers, Maît: First Captain of the Word Bearers, Master of the Faith, Priest-King of Colchis. Despised by many within his Legion, who called him a "half-Astartes", Kor Phaeron was Lorgar's adoptive father, who instilled in him the traditions of Colchis. When the XVII Legion was united with its Primarch, Kor Phaeron was too old to undergo the full implantation process, but his Primarch held him in such esteem that he received the most powerful biological augmentations available to a man of his age without making him a Space Marine, and he was appointed First Captain.

Primarque de la Death Guard, le Roi Blêm: Primarch of the Death Guard, the Pale King, the Reaper, the Grim Liberator of Barbarus. The grim and shadowed Mortarion was the Primarch and Commander of the Death Guard Legion. He grew up on a nightmarish world of horror and malefic secrets where humans were hunted like animals, and the darkness of that world crept into his soul, never to leave him. As relentless as he was determined, the reaper Primarch made his Legion into unyielding liberators, spectres of death and judgement for whom no battlefield was insurmountable and no foe too fearsome. Horus won him to his cause using lies and half-truths, and the price the Primarch and his Legion paid for their part in the Horus Heresy surpassed in horror the most unimaginable nightmares.
Primarque de la Raven Guard, Le Libérate: Primarch of the Raven Guard, The Deliverer, He Who Chooses the Slain, The Shadowed Lord.
Primarque des Emperor's Children, Le Phé: Primarch of the Emperor's Children, The Phoenician, The Prefector of Chemos. Fickle and vain, Fulgrim was the Primarch of the Emperor's Children Legion. He strove to be exemplary in all things: strategy, combat techniques, governance, reason and initiative, and passed these values on to his Legion, which enshrined them as an implacable devotion to martial perfection. Under his aegis, the Emperor's Children rose from the ashes of near-certain extinction to become the paragons of the Emperor's vision of the Legiones Astartes. Fulgrim established a clear and rigid chain of command within the Legion; his opinions, personal beliefs and desires were passed down to every echelon as a doctrine that could not be questioned. His sons, for whom he was the centre of their bloody letters, strove to imitate his example and live up to his ambitions.
Primarque des Imperial Fists, Le Vigilan: Primarch of the Imperial Fists, The Vigilant, The Emperor's Blade, Praetorian of Terra, The Unyielding.
Primarque des Night Lords, Hante-la-Nuit: Primarch of the Night Lords, the Night Haunter, the Last Judge, the King of Terrors. Nicknamed the "Night Haunter" by the inhabitants of his adoptive world of Nostramo, Konrad Curze acquired a sinister reputation from his earliest days. The Night Haunter eventually brought order back to Nostramo, instituting a reign of terror that spared neither criminals nor despots. When the Emperor finally found him, Curze had already foreseen his whole life, from his role as Primarch to his tragic end, and his reason had been badly shaken by visions of the horror that would soon engulf the galaxy. After taking command of the VIII Legion, which he named the Night Lords, Curze set about applying his methods to the galaxy. At the second request of his brother, the Warmaster, Curze joined the Traitors, a cruel lord now turned against his other brothers and their Legions.
Primarque des Thousand Sons. Parmi les P: Primarch of the Thousand Sons. Among the Primarchs, Magnus the Red was the undisputed master of the mystic arts. In psychic power he was second only to the Emperor, and some even hold that certain of his secrets were beyond his father's reach. Magnus the Red was the archetype of the warrior-philosopher and the embodiment of considered action: his presence was a constant reminder to his sons not to give in to impulsiveness, and to conduct their campaigns with the same care and the same measure of doubt as their psychic meditations.
Primarque des Ultramarines, Le Victorieu: Primarch of the Ultramarines, The Victorious, The Master of Ultramar, Regent of Hosts, The Blade of Unity.
Primarque des White Scars, Le Faucon, Ma: Primarch of the White Scars, The Warhawk, Master of the Azure Firmament.
Primarque des Word Bearers, L'Aurélien,: Primarch of the Word Bearers, The Aurelian, The Golden One, The Voice of Truth. Lorgar Aurelian, the Golden Son, who alone among his brothers wielded the power of devotion as a weapon, was the lord of the Word Bearers Legion. He conquered worlds by the sheer force of his words and charisma, converting them to the worship of the Emperor, whom he saw as Humanity's divine saviour.

Quand ils Chargent, les World Eaters ont: When they Charge, World Eaters gain a +1 bonus to their Attacks Characteristic.
Quand ils doivent combattre dans des esp: When they must fight in confined spaces, veterans who favour close combat forgo the cumbersome Jump Packs more often carried in engagements on open ground. Adopting a more aggressive doctrine than their brothers assigned to conventional Destroyer Squads, these Legionaries find themselves in the thick of the melee, exacting a heavy toll on their enemies.
Quand la figurine explose, toute unité à: When the model explodes, every unit within 6" suffers a number of Hit Tests equal to the Base Wounds of the exploding model (Strength 8, Damage 1).
Quand le Lion décrète qu'un monde doit p: When the Lion decrees that a world must die, he entrusts command of that grim operation to the veterans of the Dreadwing. This Detachment's Support Slots may only be used to select Dreadwing Interemptors Units or Rapier Battery Units.
Quand le Lion partait au combat, rares é: When the Lion went to war, few were the foes worthy of perishing by his hand, and only those who show a virulence equal to his hostility witness the true wrath of the First Primarch. The Lion gains a bonus to the Focus Roll when wounded. While a Model with this Special Rule is Engaged in a Challenge, if it has 2 Wounds or fewer remaining, its Controlling Player may choose this Gambit: The Lion's Wrath — if this Gambit is chosen, the Controlling Player of this Model adds a modifier of +2 to the Focus Roll, and does not suffer the -1 modifier per point of difference between this Model's Base Wounds Characteristic and its Current Wounds Characteristic.
Quand les Blood Angels Chargent avec suc: When Blood Angels Charge successfully, the Strength of their Attacks increases.
Quand les Iron Warriors libérèrent le ph: When the Iron Warriors unleashed the phage on Tallarn, plains and savannahs dissolved into seething rot and the forests collapsed into foul quagmires. Within an hour, Tallarn's biosphere was dead.
Quand les Templiers des Serments de la L: When the Legion's Templars of the Oaths go to war, nothing can stop them: the Templars strike with the lashing force of a tidal wave of power armour, a tactic hardly subtle but whose irresistible method has proved its effectiveness time and again. Templar Brethren launch their assault more effectively when they charge after Disembarking. In the Assault Phase of any Player Turn in which they Disembarked from an Assault Vehicle, Models with this Special Rule may add +2" to their Set-up Move. This modifier does not apply if the Unit was forced to make an Emergency Disembarkation in the same Turn.
Quand on alloue une Blessure à une Figur: When a Wound is allocated to a Model equipped with a Coriolis pattern power shield, the Damage Characteristic of the Unsaved Wound is modified by -1 (to a minimum of 1). In addition, a Model equipped with a Coriolis pattern power shield gains the Shield Trait.
Quand on choisit cette Posture, la Figur: When this Gambit is chosen, the Model adopting it gains double the normal bonus to its Focus Roll from any Outside Support it benefits from. In addition, while it adopts this Gambit, its opponent can gain at most a +2 bonus from their own Outside Support.
Quand on choisit cette Posture, on rédui: When this Gambit is chosen, the Combat Initiative of the Opposing Player's Model is reduced.
Quand on déclare des vœux Questoris pour: When declaring Questoris vows for an army with the Landless Company household paradigm, the Vow of Belligerence may be declared in addition to the common Questoris vows. Unlike other Questoris vows, the Vow of Belligerence may be declared for a single model with the Knight sub-type in an army that does not use the Knight Households Primary Detachment, but that otherwise follows all the standard rules for declaring Questoris vows.
When declaring Questoris vows for an army with the Imperial House household paradigm, the Vow of Domination may be declared in addition to the common Questoris vows.
When declaring Questoris vows for an army with the Mechanicum Vassals household paradigm, the Vow of Obedience may be declared in addition to the common Questoris vows.
Quand on effectue une Réaction Répliquer: When a Return Fire Reaction is made for a Model with this Special Rule, all of its Turret Mounted Weapons are treated as Defensive Weapons regardless of their Characteristics. If a Turret Mounted Weapon of a Model with this Special Rule is already a Defensive Weapon, the Model's Controlling Player may instead add +1 to Hit Tests made for that Weapon's Fire Group when making this Reaction.
Quand on fait un Jet de Blessure pour un: When making a Wound Test for an Attack with this Special Rule, if the result is equal to or greater than the value of X attached to this variant of the Special Rule (ignoring modifiers), the Wounds inflicted ignore the Target Model's Eternal Warrior (X) Special Rule.
Quand on fait un Test pour éviter de gag: When making a Check to avoid gaining a Tactical Status for a Unit that includes at least one Model with this Special Rule, the Controlling Player must roll an additional dice, discarding the dice with the highest result if the Check is made in the Morale Sub-Phase, or the dice with the lowest result if the Check is made in the Resolution Sub-Phase.
Quand on fait une Attaque de Tir pour un: When making a Shooting Attack for a Unit composed only of Models with this Special Rule, add +1 to the result of Hit Tests made for the attacks of any Fire Group that totals more than five Dice or attacks and has the Bolt or Auto Trait.
Quand on rate un test de résistance cont: When a Resistance Check against a psychic Curse is failed: a model with the Psyker trait and Line of Sight to the target unit (or to the Curse's Focus) may attempt to nullify it. Subtract the Focus's Willpower from our model's Willpower, then make a Willpower Check with the power's modifier. Passed: the Curse fails. Failed: it is resolved normally.
Quand on résout un Combat à la Sous-phas: When resolving a Combat in the Resolution Sub-phase of the Assault Phase, score 1 Combat Resolution Point if at least one friendly Model involved in that Combat has the Word Bearers Trait.
Quand on sélectionne des Unités dans un: When selecting Units in a Primary, Allied or Lord of War Detachment, the selected Units must have a variant of the Mechanicum Faction Trait, but they need not have the same variant as the other Units in the same Detachment. However, all Units in the same Auxiliary or Apex Detachment selected from this Army List must have the same variant.
Quand on sélectionne un trait de faction: When a Faction Trait is selected to replace the [Questoris Familia] trait, a corresponding household paradigm is automatically selected, which confers a range of special rules and effects. The three household paradigms (Questoris Imperialis, Questoris Mechanicum and Questoris Mendicus) are detailed in the following sections.
Quand on utilise ce Détachement Principa: When using this Primary Detachment, ignore the limits on the amount or percentage of army points to be spent on Lords of War in all of the army's detachments; a player is allowed to spend all the points available for selecting an army that includes this Primary Detachment on a single Lord of War choice!
Quand survint l'apothéose de Fulgrim, la: By the time of Fulgrim's apotheosis, the perversion of his Legion was already notorious among allies and enemies alike. Fulgrim Transfigured cannot be included in the same Army as Fulgrim.
Quand un monde meurt à petit feu, la val: When a world is slowly dying, the worth of a position is measured less by what it protects than by those who still refuse to abandon it.
Quand un Mortificator est amené à combat: When a Mortificator is called upon to fight as guardian of the Dreadnoughts they oversee, the increased resilience of Terminator plate is often all but vital, for Dreadnoughts are machines built for the most intense fighting. Those who choose such panoply tend to be the most belligerent of their peers, hurling themselves into the heart of the melee alongside their towering charges rather than remaining behind as a support element. This Model may be replaced by 1 Mortificator Tartaros for free.
Quand un objectif progresse, sa valeur a: When an objective advances, its value increases by 1, to a maximum of 3, then it moves one sector towards the Defender's edge. It can never move diagonally. If no move is possible, it stays in place but can still gain +1 value, again to a maximum of 3.
Quand une Arme ayant cette Règle Spécial: When a Weapon with this Special Rule is selected for a Model during a Challenge, the Controlling Player may select a successful Hit Test made by the opposing Player with a result of 6, and set its result to 1.
When a Weapon with this Special Rule is used, all of the Model's other Weapons are reduced to Snap Shots for the rest of the Shooting Attack.

When a Weapon with this Special Rule makes a Shooting Attack, the attacking Player may choose to target any point on the battlefield within range, ignoring Line of Sight and without needing to target an enemy Model. The Hit Test is made as normal, but once the final position of the Template has been determined, the Attacking Player resolves no Hits, whether or not any Models are under the Template, and must instead choose one of the following two options: Emerge or Tunnel. If they choose to Tunnel, the Template remains in place, but no Hits are resolved and the Template has no effect on Line of Sight, Movement or any other aspect of the game — it simply marks the position of the macro-drill, buried deep underground. At the start of the Controlling Player's next Shooting Phase, they must again choose to Tunnel or Emerge. If they choose to Tunnel again, the Template may then be moved up to 36" in any direction, and again remains in place until the Controlling Player's next Shooting Phase. Emerge may only be chosen if no part of the Template is touching Impassable Terrain. Once this choice has been made, all enemy Models wholly or partially covered by the Template suffer a wound with an AP of 2 and a Damage of 1, and all enemy Models not covered by the Template but within 2" of any point on its edge suffer a Hit at Strength 6 with an AP of 4 and a Damage of 1. If a Unit suffers one or more Casualties as a result of either of these effects, a Cool Check must be made for that Unit; if it is failed, all Models in that Unit gain the Stunned Status. Once all Hits and wounds have been fully resolved, enemy Models wholly or partially covered by the Template are moved by their Controlling Player the shortest possible distance so that they are no longer covered by the Template. The Controlling Player of the seismic macro-drill may then choose to Disembark some or all of the Units Embarked on the seismic macro-drill, using any point of the Template as an Access Point. Models disembarked in this way may be placed on the Template. The Template then remains in place, and any Model still Embarked on the seismic macro-drill may Disembark from it in a later Movement Phase as usual, but may not Embark on it again. The Template remains in place until all Models have Disembarked from the seismic macro-drill; it does not block Line of Sight, does not impede Movement, and is not considered to be any type of Terrain. Although it is a Strategic Weapon, a Weapon with this Special Rule cannot be used to target Strategic Objectives.
Quand une Figurine ayant cette Règle Spé: When a Model with this Special Rule is the Target of a Charge, in Step 4 of the Charge Procedure, a Model with this Special Rule may make an additional Volley Attack. This additional Volley Attack is made as a separate Shooting Attack, after its first Volley Attack has been resolved, and the Controlling Player may only select a Pintle Weapon to make attacks during this second Volley Attack. If any Models are Removed as a Casualty as a result of this Model's Shooting Attacks during this Volley Attack, the Charging Unit subtracts 1 from the result of any Charge Roll made this Phase.
When a Model with this Special Rule makes Volley Attacks, it is not reduced to making Snap Shots.
When a Model with this Special Rule is allocated an Unsaved Wound from a Shooting Attack, the Damage of that Unsaved Wound is reduced by 1, to a minimum of 1.
Quand une Figurine de cette Unité fait u: When a Model in this Unit makes a Shooting Attack with a bolter, the bolter gains the Heavy (FP) Special Rule until the Shooting Attack has been fully resolved.
Quand une mobilité accrue est requise, l: When greater mobility is required, Praetors often choose to wage war astride a Scimitar Jetbike or Spatha Jetbike. Offering unmatched additional speed and firepower, these powerful mounts allow a Praetor to respond swiftly to threats across the whole battlefront, bringing their skill and expertise wherever it is needed. While the wargear they can carry into battle is limited, the ability to close on the foe at speed like the cavalry of antiquity more than makes up for this drawback, and the most skilled riders know how to bring their heavy weaponry into range before charging the survivors, blade in hand.
Quand une Unité composée uniquement de F: When a Unit composed only of Models with this Special Rule is the target of a Shooting Attack, all attacks must be made as Snap Shots if the distance between the Target Unit and the closest Model of the Attacking Unit is 18" or more.
When a Unit composed only of Models with this Special Rule fails a Leadership Test, its Controlling Player may make it Lost to the Nails.
Quand une Unité de Mortificator ou de Mo: When a Mortificator or Mortificator in Terminator Armour Unit is selected to fill a Command Force Organisation Slot, the Controlling Player may choose to add a Dreadnought Talon Auxiliary Detachment to the Army instead of the options normally available in the Crusade Force Organisation Chart. The War-engines Slots of this Detachment may only be used to select Contemptor Dreadnought Units.
Quand une Unité devient Livrée aux Clous: When a Unit becomes Lost to the Nails, all Tactical Statuses affecting it are removed. In addition, while a Unit is Lost to the Nails: Models in the Unit may add +1" to the distance covered during a Set-up Move; the value of the Attacks Characteristic of Models in the Unit is modified by +1; Models in the Unit are treated as having a Leadership, Cool and Willpower Characteristic of 10 (unless it is normally higher); at the start of the Controlling Player's Charge Sub-phase, if it is within 12" of any enemy Model, the Unit must make a Charge Move (if there are several enemy Units within 12", the Unit's Controlling Player must nominate the closest enemy Unit).
Quand une Unité devient Stupéfiée, on re: When a Unit becomes Stupefied, all Tactical Statuses affecting it are removed. In addition, while a Unit is Stupefied: Models in the Unit have the Feel No Pain (6+) Special Rule; the Strength Characteristic of Models in the Unit is modified by +1; Models in the Unit cannot gain any Tactical Status; the Controlling Player of a Stupefied Unit may not declare any Reactions for that Unit, and must make all Shooting Attacks for it as Snap Shots; in the Effects Sub-phase of the End Phase, the Controlling Player must make a Cool Test for each Stupefied Unit in their Army — if the Test is passed, that Unit is no longer Stupefied.
Quand une unité du Défenseur arrive des: When one of the Defender's units arrives from Reserves, the Defender may choose to have it enter from one of the short edges of the table instead of their usual edge.
Quand une unité ennemie arrive à 12 pouc: When an enemy unit comes within 12": an immediate move up to the unit's Initiative. Useful for taking cover or improving your position.
Quand une Unité entièrement composée de: When a Unit composed entirely of Models of the Malefic Sub-type that includes at least one Model with this item of Wargear would gain any Tactical Status, that Unit instead suffers 1 automatic wound with a Damage Characteristic of 1, against which no Saves of any kind may be made, instead of the D3 wounds normally inflicted by the Malefic Sub-type.
Quand une Unité qui comprend une Figurin: When a Unit that includes a Model with this Special Rule is declared as the Target Unit of a Charge, or the Target Unit of a Reaction or Advanced Reaction, the Controlling Player of the Unit for which the Charge or Reaction is declared must make a Leadership Check. If the Check is passed, the Charge or Reaction is resolved normally. If the Check is failed, the Unit for which the Charge or Reaction was declared immediately gains the Stunned Status and the Controlling Player cannot declare any other Charge or Reaction for that Unit during that Phase, but their remaining Reaction Allotment is not reduced.
Quand vous ajoutez une unité à votre arm: When you add a unit to your army, you must choose one of the following traits — this choice replaces every instance of the [Questoris Familia] trait:
Quand, à l'étape Déclarer les Armes et D: When, in the Declare Weapons and Set Initiative Steps step of the Fight Sub-Phase, a Weapon with this Special Rule is chosen to make Attacks, all Models with the [Skitarii] Trait that belong to the same Unit as the Model with a Weapon with this Special Rule are immediately relieved of the Pinned, Suppressed and Stunned Tactical Statuses.
Quatre objectifs représentant des <stron: Four objectives representing refinery platforms are placed on the table.
Quatre quarts de table, quatre objectifs: Four table quarters, four objectives whose value depends on who holds the sector.
Que ce soit par dissimulation optique, r: Whether by optical concealment, hidden lairs or simply by slipping out of sight, many forces use subterfuge to ambush their enemy. This Special Rule allows Models to use an Advanced Reaction to arrive from Reserves in close proximity to an enemy Unit. The Controlling Player of a Unit that includes only Models with this Special Rule may use the Concealed Ambush Advanced Reaction.
Quel que soit le statut tactique, une un: Whatever the Tactical Status, a unit suffers the following penalties: Disordered charge; combat Initiative of 1; neither controls nor contests objectives and no "Stationary" benefit.
Quota Seigneur de Guerre + Seigneur des: Warlord + Lord of War allowance exceeded:
Raids des Emperor’s Children sur les raf: Emperor’s Children raids on the promethium refineries, until the VII<sup>th</sup> Legion intervenes.
Rancuniers et increvables, les fils de P: Bitter and indestructible, the sons of Perturabo know only siege warfare: stone by stone, bastion by bastion, until victory.
Rann est réputé pour son talent singulie: Rann is renowned for his singular talent for combining the use of his axes and a shield. Fafnir Rann suffers no penalty in a Challenge for carrying a shield. The Controlling Player of a Model with this Special Rule does not suffer the -1 penalty to Focus Rolls for that Model having the Heavy Sub-type.
Rapide + Transport qui Fonce : personne: Fast + Transport that Rushes: no one disembarks that turn (except by Emergency Disembarkation).
Rares en dehors des rangs de formations: Rare outside the ranks of particularly esoteric formations or certain specific Legions, a handful of Forge Lords take the field astride a Spatha bike or Scimitar Jetbike, whether to accompany the swift armour whose advance they escort or to make their warrior-artisan skills more readily available.
Raven Guard — Maîtres de l’Occultation <: Raven Guard — Masters of Obfuscation ❯
Raven Guard. Si les Raven Guard ont été: Raven Guard. If the Raven Guard were chosen for the Army's Shattered Legions Detachments, a Model subject to the Mutable Tactics Special Rule that does not remain Stationary in its Controlling Player's Movement Sub-Phase gains the Shrouded (6+) Special Rule until the start of its Controlling Player's next Turn — a Special Rule distinct from the Shrouded Damage Mitigation Roll already described on this site.
Réacteurs modèle Corvidé (Mouvement fixé: Corvid Pattern Jump Pack (Movement set to 14, Bulky (X) replaced by Bulky (3), Dangerous Terrain Tests automatically passed)
Réaction Avancée : <span class=\"regle-t: Advanced Reaction: <span class="regle-tag" tabindex="0" >Bring It Down!<span class="tooltip" >The Reactive Player may declare it at the end of Step 5 of a successful Charge by the Active Player whose Charging Unit includes a Walker/Automata Type Model or a Malefic Sub-type Model with Bulky (3) or more, against a Target Unit made up solely of Models with the Solar Auxilia Trait (cost: 1 Reaction Allotment): each Model in the Reacting Unit with a Weapon that has the Detonation Special Rule immediately attacks the Charging Unit as if Engaged with it at that Initiative Step, with the Casualties inflicted counting towards Combat Resolution.</span ></span >.

Advanced Reaction: <span class="regle-tag" tabindex="0" >Cerebral Augmentations<span class="tooltip" >The Reactive Player may declare it during the Morale Sub-Phase of the Shooting Phase, or at the Make Panic Checks Step of the Assault Phase, when a Unit under their control made up solely of Infantry Type Models with the Solar Auxilia Trait but not the Bulky (X) Special Rule would gain the Routed Status (cost: 1 Reaction Allotment): the Unit does not gain that Status, but immediately suffers D3 automatic wounds ignoring Armour and Cover Saves (Invulnerable Saves and Damage Mitigation Rolls allowed).</span ></span >.

Advanced Reaction: <span class="regle-tag" tabindex="0" >Fog of War<span class="tooltip" >The Reactive Player may declare it during the Morale Sub-Phase of the Shooting Phase, when a Unit under their control made up solely of Infantry Type Models with the Solar Auxilia Trait would gain the Routed Status after a failed Leadership Check (cost: 1 Reaction Allotment): the Unit does not gain that Status, but immediately gains the Negligence and Impact (A) Special Rules for the rest of the Battle, and loses any version of Line (X) as well as any Infantry/Veteranis/Artillery Tercio Traits.</span ></span >.

Advanced Reaction: <span class="regle-tag" tabindex="0" >Psychic Shock<span class="tooltip" >The Reactive Player may declare it in the Shooting Phase, at the end of Step 11 of a Shooting Attack by the Active Player that would cause a Panic Check for Casualties against a Unit under their control made up solely of Infantry Type Models with the Solar Auxilia Trait but not the Bulky (X) Special Rule (cost: 1 Reaction Allotment): the Reacting Unit immediately suffers a result from the Perils of the Warp Table, then another result from the Perils of the Warp Table is immediately resolved against the Unit that made the Shooting Attack, before the Active Player's Shooting Phase continues normally.</span ></span >.

Advanced Reaction: <span class="regle-tag" tabindex="0" >Combined Arms<span class="tooltip" >The Reactive Player may declare it at the start of Step 3 of a Shooting Attack by the Active Player against a Unit under their control made up solely of Models with the Solar Auxilia Trait (cost: 1 Reaction Allotment). The Reacting Unit immediately makes a Shooting Attack against the Attacking Unit; if it causes it to lose at least one Wound after Saves and Mitigation, the latter's Charge immediately becomes a Disordered Charge.</span ></span >.

Advanced Reaction: <span class="regle-tag" tabindex="0" >Counter-assault<span class="tooltip" >The Reactive Player may declare it at Step 2 of the Reposition Sub-Phase, when an enemy Unit ends its move within 6 inches of and in Line of Sight of a Unit under their control made up solely of Infantry Type Models with the Solar Auxilia Trait but not the Bulky (X) Special Rule (cost: 1 Reaction Allotment): the Reacting Unit immediately makes a Charge Roll against that enemy Unit, with no Cool Check if it fails.</span ></span >.

Advanced Reaction: <span class="regle-tag" tabindex="0" >Reposition<span class="tooltip" >The Reactive Player may declare it at the start of Step 4 of the Charge process of any Charge declared by the Active Player that targets a Unit under their control made up solely of Infantry Type Models with the Solar Auxilia Trait but not the Bulky (X) Special Rule (cost: 1 Reaction Allotment): the Reacting Unit moves up to its Initiative Characteristic in inches in Coherency, then makes a Volley Attack against the Unit that declared the Charge, its Ranged Weapons gaining the Assault Trait for the occasion, before the Active Player moves on normally to Step 4 of the Charge.</span ></span >.

Advanced Reaction: <span class="regle-tag" tabindex="0" >Diversion<span class="tooltip" >The Reactive Player may declare it at Step 3 of a Shooting Attack by the Active Player against a Unit under their control made up solely of Infantry Type Models with the Solar Auxilia Trait but not the Bulky (X) Special Rule (cost: 1 Reaction Allotment), if another friendly Unit without Bulky (X) is within 12 inches and within range of all the Weapons declared by the Active Player: the Active Player must immediately take a Cool Check for the original Target Unit; if it fails, the Shooting Attack continues against that other Unit, which becomes the Target in its place.</span ></span >.

Advanced Reaction: <span class="regle-tag" tabindex="0" >Endure the Torment<span class="tooltip" >The Reactive Player may declare it during the Morale Sub-Phase of the Shooting Phase, when a Unit under their control made up solely of Infantry or Cavalry Type Models with the Solar Auxilia Trait would gain the Pinned, Stunned or Suppressed Tactical Status after a failed Characteristic Test (cost: 1 Reaction Allotment): the Unit does not gain that Status, as if the Test had been passed.</span ></span >.

Advanced Reaction: <span class="regle-tag" tabindex="0" >Hunter's Strike<span class="tooltip" >Once per Battle, the Reactive Player may declare it for free when an enemy Unit finishes entering play from Reserves in Line of Sight of a Unit under their control made up solely of Infantry Type Models with the Solar Auxilia Trait but not the Bulky (X) Special Rule: that Unit moves straight towards the enemy Unit (without being able to Rush) then makes a Charge Roll against it, with a Charge Move and becoming Locked in Combat if successful.</span ></span >.

Advanced Reaction: <span class="regle-tag" tabindex="0" >Warmaster's Harangue<span class="tooltip" >The Reactive Player may declare it during the Rout Sub-Phase of the Movement Phase, when a Unit under their control made up solely of Models with the Solar Auxilia Trait makes its Fall Back Move (cost: 1 Reaction Allotment): that Unit makes a move towards one or more nearby enemy Units instead of Rushing normally, then each friendly Unit made up solely of Models with the Solar Auxilia Trait within 12 inches may in turn move a number of inches equal to its Initiative Characteristic, in Coherency, this move counting as a Reaction in that Battle Turn.</span ></span >.

Advanced Reaction: <span class="regle-tag" tabindex="0" >The Butcher's Due<span class="tooltip" >The Reactive Player may declare it during the Resolution Sub-Phase of the Assault Phase, when an enemy Unit moves as part of a Disengage or Fall Back Aftermath option and is in Line of Sight of a Unit under their control made up solely of Models with the Solar Auxilia Trait that are not Locked in Combat (cost: 1 Reaction Allotment): the Reacting Unit immediately makes a Shooting Attack against that enemy Unit only.</span ></span >.

Advanced Reaction: <span class="regle-tag" tabindex="0" >Endure<span class="tooltip" >The Reactive Player may declare it in the Shooting Phase, at the end of Step 11 of a Shooting Attack by the Active Player that would cause a Panic Check for Casualties against a Unit under their control made up solely of Infantry Type Models with the Solar Auxilia Trait but not the Bulky (X) Special Rule (cost: 1 Reaction Allotment), to avoid that Check: the Reacting Unit then makes a Snap Shot Shooting Attack against an enemy Unit in Line of Sight chosen by the Reactive Player, then the avoided Panic Check is resolved normally.</span ></span >.

Advanced Reaction: <span class="regle-tag" tabindex="0" >Redouble<span class="tooltip" >The Reactive Player may declare it during the Morale Sub-Phase of the Shooting Phase, when a Unit under their control made up solely of Infantry Type Models with the Solar Auxilia Trait but not the Bulky (X) Special Rule passes a Cool or Leadership Check to avoid a Tactical Status (cost: 1 Reaction Allotment): that Unit makes a standard Reposition move (without Rushing), then each friendly non-Vehicle Unit with the Solar Auxilia Trait within 12 inches may in turn move a number of inches equal to its Initiative Characteristic, this move counting as a Reaction in that Battle Turn.</span ></span >.

Advanced Reaction: <span class="regle-tag" tabindex="0" >Impregnable Bulwark<span class="tooltip" >The Reactive Player may declare it at the start of Step 3 of a Shooting Attack by the Active Player against a Unit under their control made up solely of Models with the Solar Auxilia Trait but not the Bulky (X) Special Rule, the majority of which benefit from a Cover Save (cost: 1 Reaction Allotment): all Models in the Reacting Unit gain +1 Toughness (up to a maximum of 4) for the duration of that Shooting Phase.</span ></span >.

Advanced Reaction: <span class="regle-tag" tabindex="0" >Chosen Ground<span class="tooltip" >Once per Battle, the Reactive Player may declare it for free during the Resolution Sub-Phase of the Assault Phase, when a Panic Check is failed for a Unit under their control made up solely of Infantry Type Models with the Solar Auxilia Trait, at least one Model of which is within 3 inches of an Objective: the Unit does not gain the Routed Status, and the Battle moves directly to the Aftermath Step, where the Reactive Player must declare the Hold option for that Unit.</span ></span >.

Réaction Avancée : Maréchal Élu <span cl: Advanced Reaction: Chosen Marshal ❯
Réaction Avancée accessible au Joueur en: Advanced Reaction available to the Controlling Player of any Unit that includes only Models with the Slaanesh Trait: allows the Reacting Unit to move when it is the target of an enemy Shooting Attack, and its surviving Models gain +1 Initiative. Trigger: once per Turn, the Reactive Player may declare it during the Shooting Phase, in Step 11 of any Shooting Attack made by the Active Player, after the Casualties caused by that Attack have been removed; it cannot be triggered by a Shooting Attack made only with Weapons that have the Disintegrator Trait. Cost: 1 point of Reaction Allotment. Target: the Unit whose Shooting Attack triggered the Reaction; the Reacting Unit is always the Target Unit of that Shooting Attack. Process: the Reactive Player rolls a dice; each Model in the Reacting Unit may be moved a distance in inches up to the result. Once the Unit has moved, all its Models gain an additional +1 modifier to their Initiative until the end of their Controlling Player's next Player Turn.
Réaction Avancée de la Désignation de Le: Advanced Reaction of the Ambaxtoi of Barbarus Legiones Auxilia Designation (XIV Legion, Death Guard). The Reactive Player may declare it in the Shooting Phase, at the end of Step 11 of a Shooting Attack by the Active Player that would cause a Panic Check for Casualties against a Unit under their control composed only of Models with the Infantry Type that have the Solar Auxilia Trait but not the Bulky (X) Special Rule (cost: 1 Reaction Allotment), to avoid that Check: the Reacting Unit then makes a Snap Shot Shooting Attack against an enemy Unit in Line of Sight of the Reactive Player's choice, then the avoided Panic Check is resolved as normal.

Advanced Reaction of the Calibanite Hunters Legiones Auxilia Designation (I Legion, Dark Angels). The Reactive Player may declare it at the end of Step 5 of a successful Charge by the Active Player whose Charging Unit includes a Model with the Walker/Automata Type or the Malefic Sub-type with Bulky (3) or higher, against a Target Unit composed only of Models that have the Solar Auxilia Trait (cost: 1 Reaction Allotment): each Model in the Reacting Unit equipped with a Weapon with the Detonation Special Rule immediately attacks the Charging Unit as if Engaged with it at that Initiative Step, with Casualties inflicted counting towards Combat Resolution.

Advanced Reaction of the Cthonian Headhunters Legiones Auxilia Designation (XVI Legion, Sons of Horus). The Reactive Player may declare it in the Rout Sub-Phase of the Movement Phase, when a Unit under their control composed only of Models that have the Solar Auxilia Trait makes its Fall Back Move (cost: 1 Reaction Allotment): that Unit makes a Move towards one or more nearby enemy Units instead of Rushing as normal, then each friendly Unit composed only of Models with the Solar Auxilia Trait within 12" may in turn Move a number of inches equal to its Initiative Characteristic, in Coherency, this Move counting as a Reaction this Battle Turn.

Advanced Reaction of the Nostraman Damnatii Legiones Auxilia Designation (VIII Legion, Night Lords). The Reactive Player may declare it in the Morale Sub-Phase of the Shooting Phase, when a Unit under their control composed only of Models with the Infantry Type that have the Solar Auxilia Trait would gain the Routed Status after a failed Leadership Check (cost: 1 Reaction Allotment): the Unit does not gain that Status, but immediately gains the Negligence and Impact (A) Special Rules for the rest of the Battle, and loses any version of Line (X) as well as any Infantry Tercio/Veteranis/Artillery Tercio Traits it has.

Advanced Reaction of the Saiphan Elevatii Legiones Auxilia Designation (IX Legion, Blood Angels). The Reactive Player may declare it in Step 2 of the Move Sub-Phase, when an enemy Unit ends its Move within 6" of and in Line of Sight of a Unit under their control composed only of Models with the Infantry Type that have the Solar Auxilia Trait but not the Bulky (X) Special Rule (cost: 1 Reaction Allotment): the Reacting Unit immediately makes a Charge Roll against that enemy Unit, with no Cool Check if it fails.

Advanced Reaction of the Prosperine Spireguard Legiones Auxilia Designation (XV Legion, Thousand Sons). The Reactive Player may declare it in the Shooting Phase, at the end of Step 11 of a Shooting Attack by the Active Player that would cause a Panic Check for Casualties against a Unit under their control composed only of Models with the Infantry Type that have the Solar Auxilia Trait but not the Bulky (X) Special Rule (cost: 1 Reaction Allotment): the Reacting Unit immediately suffers a result from the Perils of the Warp Table, then another result from the Perils of the Warp Table is immediately resolved against the Unit that made the Shooting Attack, before the Active Player's Shooting Phase continues as normal.

Advanced Reaction of the High Guard of Ultramar Legiones Auxilia Designation (XIII Legion, Ultramarines). The Reactive Player may declare it at the start of Step 3 of a Shooting Attack by the Active Player against a Unit under their control composed only of Models that have the Solar Auxilia Trait (cost: 1 Reaction Allotment). The Reacting Unit immediately makes a Shooting Attack against the Charging Unit; if it causes that Unit to lose at least one Wound after Saves and Mitigation, the latter's Charge immediately becomes a Disordered Charge.

Advanced Reaction of the Fenrisian Kaerls Legiones Auxilia Designation (VI Legion, Space Wolves). Once per Battle, the Reactive Player may declare it at no cost when an enemy Unit finishes entering play from Reserves in Line of Sight of a Unit under their control composed only of Models with the Infantry Type that have the Solar Auxilia Trait but not the Bulky (X) Special Rule: that Unit Moves straight towards the enemy Unit (without being able to Rush) and then makes a Charge Roll against it, making a Charge Move and becoming Locked in Combat if successful.

Advanced Reaction of the Chogorian Limitanei Legiones Auxilia Designation (V Legion, White Scars). Once per Battle, the Reactive Player may declare it at no cost in the Resolution Sub-Phase of the Assault Phase, when a Panic Check is failed for a Unit under their control composed only of Models with the Infantry Type that have the Solar Auxilia Trait, with at least one Model within 3" of an Objective: the Unit does not gain the Routed Status, and the Battle proceeds directly to the Aftermath Step, where the Reactive Player must declare the Hold option for that Unit.

Advanced Reaction of the Archite Palatines Legiones Auxilia Designation (III Legion, Emperor's Children). The Reactive Player may declare it in the Morale Sub-Phase of the Shooting Phase, when a Unit under their control composed only of Models with the Infantry Type that have the Solar Auxilia Trait but not the Bulky (X) Special Rule passes a Cool or Leadership Check to avoid a Tactical Status (cost: 1 Reaction Allotment): that Unit makes a standard Move (without Rushing), then each friendly non-Vehicle Unit with the Solar Auxilia Trait within 12" may in turn Move a number of inches equal to its Initiative Characteristic, this Move counting as a Reaction this Battle Turn.

Advanced Reaction of the Inwit Phalangites Legiones Auxilia Designation (VII Legion, Imperial Fists). The Reactive Player may declare it at the start of Step 3 of a Shooting Attack by the Active Player against a Unit under their control composed only of Models that have the Solar Auxilia Trait but not the Bulky (X) Special Rule, the majority of which benefit from a Cover Save (cost: 1 Reaction Allotment): all Models in the Reacting Unit gain +1 Toughness (to a maximum of 4) for the duration of that Shooting Phase.

Advanced Reaction of the Medusan Chain Shroud Legiones Auxilia Designation (X Legion, Iron Hands). The Reactive Player may declare it in the Morale Sub-Phase of the Shooting Phase, or in the Make Panic Checks Step of the Assault Phase, when a Unit under their control composed only of Models with the Infantry Type that have the Solar Auxilia Trait but not the Bulky (X) Special Rule would gain the Routed Status (cost: 1 Reaction Allotment): the Unit does not gain that Status, but immediately suffers D3 automatic wounds that ignore Armour and Cover Saves (Invulnerable Saves and Damage Mitigation Rolls are allowed).

Advanced Reaction of the Selucian Thorakites Legiones Auxilia Designation (IV Legion, Iron Warriors). The Reactive Player may declare it in the Morale Sub-Phase of the Shooting Phase, when a Unit under their control composed only of Models with the Infantry or Cavalry Type that have the Solar Auxilia Trait would gain the Pinned, Stunned or Suppressed Tactical Status after a failed Characteristic Check (cost: 1 Reaction Allotment): the Unit does not gain that Status, as if the Check had been passed.

Advanced Reaction of the Nagrakal Thraexii Legiones Auxilia Designation (XII Legion, World Eaters). The Reactive Player may declare it in the Resolution Sub-Phase of the Assault Phase, when an enemy Unit moves as part of a Disengage or Fall Back Aftermath option and is in Line of Sight of a Unit under their control composed only of Models that have the Solar Auxilia Trait and are not Locked in Combat (cost: 1 Reaction Allotment): the Reacting Unit immediately makes a Shooting Attack against that enemy Unit only.

Advanced Reaction of the Velites of Therion Legiones Auxilia Designation (XIX Legion, Raven Guard). The Reactive Player may declare it at the start of Step 4 of the Charge process of any Charge declared by the Active Player that targets a Unit under their control composed only of Models with the Infantry Type that have the Solar Auxilia Trait but not the Bulky (X) Special Rule (cost: 1 Reaction Allotment): the Reacting Unit Moves up to its Initiative Characteristic in inches, in Coherency, then makes a Volley Attack against the Unit that declared the Charge, its Ranged Weapons gaining the Assault Trait for the occasion, before the Active Player proceeds to Step 4 of the Charge as normal.

Advanced Reaction of the Sparatoi Vindictaires Legiones Auxilia Designation (XX Legion, Alpha Legion). The Reactive Player may declare it in Step 3 of a Shooting Attack by the Active Player against a Unit under their control composed only of Models with the Infantry Type that have the Solar Auxilia Trait but not the Bulky (X) Special Rule (cost: 1 Reaction Allotment), if another friendly Unit without Bulky (X) is within 12" and within range of all Weapons declared by the Active Player: the Active Player must immediately make a Cool Check for the original Target Unit; if it fails, the Shooting Attack continues against that other Unit, which becomes the Target in its place.
Réaction Avancée de la Legio Custodes qu: Legio Custodes Advanced Reaction that splits a Reacting Unit into two separate Units. Once per Battle, the Reactive Player may declare it during Step 2 of the Move Sub-Phase process if an enemy Unit ends a move within 12" and in Line of Sight of a Unit they control (cost: 1 Reaction Allotment). The Reacting Unit must be within 12" and in Line of Sight of the Target Unit, be composed only of Models that have both the Legio Custodes AND The Sodality Traits, and include at least six Models. Once the Target Unit's move has been resolved, the Reactive Player must move at least three Models of the Reacting Unit a number of inches equal to each Model's Initiative Characteristic, so that they are no longer in Unit Coherency with the rest of the Reacting Unit but remain in Unit Coherency with each other; at least three Models of the Reacting Unit must remain that have not moved and that stay in Unit Coherency with each other. The moved Models then form a new Unit, separate from the rest of the Reacting Unit in all respects, including for scoring Victory Points (except for the Last Man Standing (X) Secondary Objective). All Models that were in the Reacting Unit when the Reaction was declared are considered to have made a Reaction this Player Turn.
Réaction Avancée des Conclaves Skitarii: Skitarii Conclave Advanced Reaction that allows a fallen marshal to be replaced in an emergency. The Reactive Player, controlling Units composed only of Models that have the Skitarii Trait, may declare it once per Battle when a friendly Skitarii Combat Peregrine Marshal Model is reduced to 0 Wounds (cost: 1 Reaction Allotment, paid on declaration); the Target Unit is always a friendly Unit that has the [Skitarii] Trait and includes at least one Ordinator Model. In the End Phase of the Turn in which the Reaction was declared, the Reactive Player chooses an Ordinator Model in the Target Unit: it gains the Command Sub-type, increases its Base Weapon Skill, Attacks and Leadership Characteristics by +1, and the Controlling Player may choose one of its Melee Weapons to gain the Icon of Authority Special Rule.
Réaction avancée des Legiones Astartes,: Legiones Astartes Advanced Reaction, costs 1 Reaction Allotment. Declared at the start of step 3 of a Shooting Attack made by the opponent. If the majority of models in the targeted unit have the Smokescreen trait: Shrouded (5+) Damage Mitigation roll for the rest of the phase, against wounds, penetrating hits and glancing hits.

Legiones Astartes Advanced Reaction, costs 1 Reaction Allotment. Declared at the start of step 3 of a Shooting Attack, or step 4 of a Charge (volley attacks), made by the opponent. If the majority of models in the targeted unit have the Shield trait: +1 Toughness for the rest of the phase.

Legiones Astartes Advanced Reaction, costs 1 Reaction Allotment. Declared at step 9 of a Shooting Attack targeting a unit that includes a Medic. When removing casualties (step 11): one recovery roll for each model that has suffered an unsaved wound (except models that themselves have "Medic").

Legiones Astartes Advanced Reaction, costs 1 Reaction point. Declared at the start of step 3 of a Shooting Attack (or step 4 of a Charge), if the majority of the targeted unit has the Shield trait: +1 Toughness for the rest of the phase.

Legiones Astartes Advanced Reaction, costs 1 Reaction point. Declared at the start of step 3 of a Shooting Attack, if the majority of the targeted unit has the Smokescreen trait: Shrouded (5+) mitigation roll for the rest of the phase, against wounds, penetrating hits and glancing hits.
Legiones Astartes Advanced Reaction, costs 1 Reaction Allotment. Declared at the start of step 4 (Volley Attacks): +1 Toughness for the phase if the majority of the unit has the Shield trait.

Legiones Astartes Advanced Reaction, costs 1 Reaction point. Declared at step 9 of a Shooting Attack targeting a unit that includes a Medic. When removing casualties (step 11): one recovery roll for each model that has suffered an unsaved wound (except models that themselves have Medic).
Réaction Avancée des Solar Auxilia qui r: Solar Auxilia Advanced Reaction that closes up a Unit's ranks to grant it a temporary Invulnerable Save. The Reactive Player may declare it in the Move Sub-Phase of the Movement Phase for a Unit under their control that includes any Model with the Solar Auxilia Trait (cost: 1 Reaction Allotment). Each Model in the Reacting Unit Moves so as to end in Base Contact with at least two other Models from the same Unit; the Unit then gains a 5+ Invulnerable Save against all Shooting Attacks for the rest of the Active Player's Turn.
Réaction Avancée du Clade Vanus (Divisio: Vanus Clade (Divisio Assassinorum) Advanced Reaction that allows the Reactive Player to disrupt the placement of an enemy Flyer arriving from Aerial Reserves. Trigger: the Reactive Player may declare it during the Reserves Sub-Phase when the Active Player passes a Reserves Roll for a Unit arriving from Aerial Reserves. Cost: free. Target: the Unit in Aerial Reserves for which the Active Player has just passed that Reserves Roll. Process: (1) the Active Player must give the Target Unit a Combat Assignment; (2) before the Active Player places it on the Battlefield, the Reactive Player makes an Intelligence Check for the Reacting Unit; (3) if it is passed, the Reactive Player may, instead of the Active Player, place the Target Unit anywhere along a Battlefield Edge that is valid for its Combat Assignment — if it is failed, this Reaction has no effect; (4) in the following Movement Phase, the Active Player may immediately pivot the Target Unit before moving it normally, in accordance with its Combat Assignment.

Vanus Clade (Divisio Assassinorum) Advanced Reaction that allows the Reactive Player to attempt to Suppress or Pin a Unit arriving from Reserves. Trigger: the Reactive Player may declare it during the Movement Phase, when the Active Player deploys a Unit arriving from Reserves. Cost: free. Target: the Unit entering play from Reserves in this way, if it is within 12" and in Line of Sight of the Reactive Player. Process: the Controlling Player makes an Intelligence Check for the Reacting Unit; if it is passed, the Target Unit gains the Suppressed or Pinned Tactical Status, at the Reactive Player's choice; if it is failed, this Reaction has no effect.
Réaction Avancée du Rite de Guerre Les L: Advanced Reaction of The Shattered Legions Rite of War. Trigger: once per Battle, the Reactive Player of a Unit that includes only Models with the Shattered Legions Trait may declare it at the end of Step 5 of the Charge process, for any Charge declared by the Active Player that Targets that Unit. Cost: 1, 2 or 3 Reaction Allotments, paid upon declaration. Target: the Target Unit is always the Unit whose Charge triggered the Reaction; the Reacting Unit is always the Unit that was declared the Target of that Charge. Process: the Reactive Player declares how many Reaction Allotments they are spending. For 1 Point, the Models in the Reacting Unit gain a +1 modifier to their Toughness until the end of the Phase. For 2 Points, they also gain that same modifier, and Models attacking the Target Unit gain a +1 modifier to their Attacks until the end of the Phase. For 3 Points, Models attacking the Target Unit additionally gain a +1 modifier to their Strength, again until the end of the Phase.
Réaction Avancée qui éloigne une Unité d: Advanced Reaction that moves a Unit out of danger while a friendly Barrage Weapon returns fire. The Reactive Player may declare it in Step 3 of a Shooting Attack made by the Active Player against a Unit under their control composed only of Infantry Models that have the Solar Auxilia Trait but not the Bulky (X) Special Rule (cost: 1 Reaction Allotment). The Target Unit of the Reaction is always the Unit whose Shooting Attack triggered it. 1. Models in the Reacting Unit Move a number of inches up to their Initiative, ending in Coherency and more than 1" from any enemy Model; if none of them is then in Line of Sight and/or in Range of any Model in the Target Unit, the Active Player may not choose another target for that Unit during the current Shooting Phase. 2. Once the Reacting Player has resolved this move, they may select a single friendly Model with the Solar Auxilia Trait and a Weapon with the Barrage (X) Special Rule, within 12" of at least one Model in the Reacting Unit. That Model immediately makes a Shooting Attack against the Target Unit with a single Weapon with the Barrage (X) Special Rule, which may be made without Line of Sight in accordance with that Special Rule. If that Model has the Vehicle Type, this may be a Battle Weapon and the Model may Pivot just before making the Shooting Attack. Note that this Model's Unit still counts as having made a Reaction this Battle Turn. 3. Once this Shooting Attack has been resolved, including Removing Casualties, finish resolving the original Shooting Attack that triggered the Reaction.
Réaction Avancée qui permet à une Unité: Advanced Reaction that allows a Solar Auxilia Unit to strike back with bayonets against a failed Charge. The Reactive Player may declare it at the end of Step 5 of a Charge whose Charge Roll failed, for the Unit that was its Target, composed only of Models that have the Solar Auxilia Trait (cost: 1 Reaction Allotment): each Model in the Reacting Unit equipped with a Weapon with the Bayonet Trait makes its melee attacks against the Charging Unit at the corresponding Initiative Step, with Models Removed as Casualties counting towards Combat Resolution.
Réaction Avancée. Déclencheur : le Joueu: Advanced Reaction. Trigger: the Reactive Player may declare this Reaction during Step 2 of the Move Sub-Phase process, after an enemy Unit has completed a Move. Cost: the Reactive Player must spend 1 point of their Reaction Allotment to declare it, paid as soon as the declaration is made. Target: the Target Unit is always the Unit whose Move triggered the Reaction. The Reactive Player must select a Unit under their control that includes only Models with the Concealed Positions Special Rule and that is in Reserves; that Unit is the Reacting Unit. Process: (1) the Reactive Player selects a Model from the Reacting Unit and places it anywhere on the battlefield outside the enemy Deployment Zone, within 6" of the Unit that triggered the Reaction and at least 5" from any enemy Model, as well as 1" from any Battlefield Edge or piece of Impassable Terrain; the remaining Models are then placed in Unit Coherency with at least one other Model from the same Unit and within 6" of the first Model placed, under the same distance restrictions; any Model that cannot be placed in this way is immediately Removed as a Casualty; (2) once the Reacting Unit has been deployed, the Reactive Player may either make a Shooting Attack with it against the Unit that triggered the Reaction (as Snap Shots), or make a Disordered Charge with it, which must target that same Unit.
Réaction des Horreurs de Tzeentch. Décle: Horrors of Tzeentch Reaction. Trigger: the Reactive Player may declare it during Step 9 of any Shooting Attack whose Target Unit includes one or more Models with this Special Rule; it cannot be triggered by a Shooting Attack made only with Weapons that have the Disintegrator Trait. Cost: 1 point of Reaction Allotment. Target: the Reacting Unit is always the Unit targeted by the Shooting Attack that triggered the Reaction; a majority of its Models must have this Special Rule when it is declared. Process: in Step 11, once all Casualties from the Target Unit have been removed, two Blue Horrors are placed on the battlefield for each Pink Horror Removed as a Casualty, in Unit Coherency with a Model of the Unit that was not placed by this Reaction, and never within 1" of an enemy Model. Models that cannot be placed because of these restrictions are considered Destroyed.
Réaction Psychique (Bénédiction) de la D: Psychic Reaction (Blessing) of the Fate-weaver Discipline: allows a Unit to gain a Shrouded Damage Mitigation Roll. Trigger: the Reactive Player may declare it at the start of Step 3 of a Shooting Attack by the Active Player that targets a Unit including at least one Model with the Weaver of Fate Trait. Cost: 1 point of Reaction Allotment, paid only if the Willpower Check is passed. Focus: a Model with the Weaver of Fate Trait controlled by the Reactive Player and part of the targeted Unit. Target: the Focus's Unit. Duration: until the end of the Sub-Phase in which it was declared. Process: the Controlling Player of the Focus makes a Manifestation Check; if it is passed, all Models in the Target Unit gain a Shrouded (5+) Damage Mitigation Roll against all wounds inflicted; if it is failed, there is no effect.
Réaction Psychique (Bénédiction) qui acc: Psychic Reaction (Blessing) that increases the Toughness Characteristic of the Reacting Unit. The Reactive Player may declare it at the start of Step 3 of a Shooting Attack made by the Active Player that targets a Unit including at least one Model with the Pavoni Trait (Cost: 1 Reaction Allotment, paid only if the Willpower Check is passed). The Focus must be a Model with the Pavoni Trait in the targeted Unit; the Target is that same Unit, composed entirely of Models with the Thousand Sons Trait. If successful, its effects last until the end of the Sub-Phase: all Models in the Target Unit gain a +2 bonus to their Toughness Characteristic.
Réaction Psychique (Bénédiction) qui don: Psychic Reaction (Blessing) that gives a Unit a Shrouded Damage Mitigation Roll. The Reactive Player may declare it at the start of Step 3 of a Shooting Attack made by the Active Player that targets a Unit including at least one Model with the Raptora Trait (Cost: 1 Reaction Allotment, paid only if the Willpower Check is passed). The Focus must be a Model with the Raptora Trait in the targeted Unit; the Target is that same Unit, composed entirely of Models with the Thousand Sons Trait. If successful, its effects last until the end of the Sub-Phase: all Models in the Target Unit gain a 4+ Shrouded Damage Mitigation Roll against any Wound suffered.
Réaction Psychique (Malédiction) de la D: Psychic Reaction (Curse) of the Anathemata Discipline, restricted to Models with the Loyalist Trait: many Esoterists have learned to seal the cracks in reality and drive back the foul creatures that pour forth from the Warp. The Reactive Player may declare it at the start of Step 3 of the Charge Procedure, during a Charge declared by the Active Player for a Unit that includes at least one Model with the Malefic Sub-type (Cost: 1 Reaction Allotment, paid on declaration). The Focus must be a Model with the Anathemata Trait, under the Reactive Player's control and part of the Unit targeted by the Charge; the Target is the Charging Unit. Make a Resistance Check: if it is successful, the Target Unit cannot make a Set-up Move of more than 1", and when making its Charge Roll (Step 5 of the Charge Procedure), the dice with the highest result is discarded instead of the lowest. Effects are resolved immediately.

Though they are not initiated into the secrets of the Hexagrammaton, these recruits have nonetheless given the Dark Angels the means to wage their crusade on a broad front.
Recrutés durant les années de l'Hérésie: Recruited during the years of the Horus Heresy, many White Scars Inductii proved markedly more pragmatic than their brothers, a generation of Legionaries raised under the shadow of death. Often trained by the Imperial Fists and Blood Angels alongside their own Legion's recruitment masters, these warriors were typically deployed first within the "Kharash" vanguard formations of the contingents alongside which they fought, before joining their Legion proper.

Rejetés ou déserteurs de leur Légion d'o: Outcasts or deserters from their original Legion, the warriors of the Shattered Legions answer only to their own oaths, forged in the adversity of the Heresy.
Reliques d'une campagne génocidaire si t: Relics of a genocidal campaign so terrible that only the Wolf King and his inner circle of priests are permitted to remember it as anything other than a nightmare, these weapons degrade the flow of time when they detonate. Ymira-class stasis bombs force the Opposing Player to keep the lowest result when making a Charge Roll. When the Target Unit of an enemy Charge Move is not already Locked in Combat and includes at least one Model equipped with Ymira-class stasis bombs, any Charge Roll is made by rolling 2D6 and discarding the highest result, instead of discarding the lowest result.
Reliques de l'Antique Nuit, les grenades: Relics of Old Night, stasis grenades could not be reproduced by the Techmarines of the First Legion and were available only in small quantities, for the most desperate cases; the Lion, however, could deploy them without restriction. Stasis grenades reduce the Combat Initiative of enemies. Once per Battle, the first time a Charge succeeds against a Model equipped with stasis grenades and the Unit it has joined, the Combat Initiative of all Models in the Charging Unit is modified by -2 for the duration of the current Assault Phase. This modifier does not affect Models in the Charging Unit that are engaged in a Challenge.

Seigneur de la XVIIIe Légion aux jours p: A lord of the XVIII Legion in the days before Vulkan's return, Cassian was condemned to the eternal half-life of a Dreadnought after suffering mortal wounds in the final battle of the old Salamanders Legion. The shell in which he was entombed, forged by Vulkan himself, is unlike any other Dreadnought pattern and is capable of limited self-repair. At the Drop Site Massacre, Dracos tore into the Traitor lines, reliving his first death as the XVIII Legion once more faced annihilation. Leaving a trail of dead behind him, Dracos was stopped only by an orbital lance strike that vitrified an entire battlefield. Horus and his generals left Isstvan certain that the old warlord's life had ended with his Primarch and his Legion, and for a year Dracos lay buried in the vitrified dust of the Urgall Depression. Rescued by warriors of his own Legion who had come seeking news of Vulkan, Cassian Dracos would be reborn, torn from the dark heart of Isstvan V and returned to the battlefield. He was no longer who he had been, now capricious and unpredictable of temper, laden with an unquenchable rage and a need for vengeance. Through his brute strength and a new power over the simple animus of battle automata, he would prove a formidable thorn in the side of Horus' ambitions.

Serment du Moment. Quand le Joueur en Co: Oath of Moment. When the Controlling Player of a Unit composed entirely of Models with the Blackshields Trait, part of a Detachment with this Oath, must make a Fall Back Move in the Movement Sub-Phase, that Move may be made in any direction, including into Base Contact with enemy Models; if a Model in the Unit ends up in contact in this way, all Models in the Unit lose the Routed Tactical Status if they had it. A Model with this Special Rule gives its Controlling Player access to the Auspectre and Signum Shunt Advanced Reactions.

A Model with this Special Rule and the Transport Sub-type may have Models Embarked on it as per the normal Rules — however, Models of any Type other than Vehicle may Embark on it, and more than one Unit may be Embarked on it at the same time. Only 4 Models that have neither the Paragon Type nor the Infantry Type may be Embarked on it, and Models with a variant of the Bulky (X) Special Rule with a value of X greater than 6, or a Base Wounds Characteristic of 10 or more, cannot Embark on it at all. In addition, Models may only Embark on or Disembark from a Model with this Special Rule if it has not yet made an attack with its seismic macro-drill. Once an attack has been made with this Weapon, no more Models may Embark on or Disembark from this Model. If the seismic macro-drill of a Model with this Special Rule is destroyed or otherwise rendered inoperable, all Models Embarked on the Model suffer a Hit at Strength 8, AP3, Damage 4. Any Model not Removed as a Casualty must then make an Emergency Disembarkation.
A Model with this Special Rule gains a 5+ Invulnerable Save.
A Model with this Special Rule ignores the effects of the Fear (X) Special Rule, and can never gain the Routed Tactical Status: if it would gain it, it is Removed as a Casualty instead.
A Model with this Special Rule ignores negative modifiers to its Characteristics caused by the loss of Wounds.

A Model with this Special Rule is never Removed as a Casualty when it Falls Back to a Battlefield Edge, and is more likely to lose the Routed Tactical Status in the End Phase. When one or more Models in a Unit composed entirely of Models with this Special Rule come into contact with a Battlefield Edge of the Controlling Player's Deployment Zone as part of a Fall Back Move, that Unit immediately loses the Routed Tactical Status and gains the Suppressed Tactical Status. In addition, when a Leadership Check is made in the Statuses Sub-Phase of the End Phase to remove the Routed Tactical Status from a Unit composed entirely of Models with this Special Rule, the Controlling Player may roll an additional dice, discarding the dice with the highest result.

A Model with this Special Rule is not required to make its Volley Attacks as Snap Shots: it fires normally. In addition, after making Volley Attacks in Step 4 of the Charge Procedure, a Unit that includes any Model with this Special Rule is not required to make a Charge Roll in Step 5. If the Controlling Player chooses not to make a Charge Roll in that Step, the Charge ends immediately.

A Model with this Special Rule does not block Line of Sight, and cannot be chosen as the Target of a Shooting Attack while another non-Automata Model in its Unit is closer to the firer and in Line of Sight.

A Model with this Special Rule cannot be targeted by Shooting Attacks or Charges, unless it has already attacked during the Battle or an enemy Unit has passed an Intelligence Check to that end. A Unit composed only of Models with this Special Rule cannot be chosen as the Target of a Shooting Attack or a Charge. When an enemy Unit completes a move within 3" of a Model with this Special Rule, the Controlling Player of the enemy Unit may make an Intelligence Check for that Unit; if it is passed, this Special Rule no longer has any effect on that Model for the rest of the Battle.

A Model with this Special Rule may target a friendly Unit with a Shooting Attack, and the targeted Unit loses the Routed Tactical Status. At the start of the Move Sub-Phase, the Controlling Player of a Model with this Special Rule may choose a Unit in their Army with the Routed Tactical Status that is within 12" of the Model with this Special Rule. If they do, the Model with this Special Rule immediately makes a Shooting Attack that targets only the chosen Unit, using only the Banestrike bolt cannon. This Shooting Attack does not cause any Leadership Checks. Once this Shooting Attack has been resolved, the Target Unit loses the Routed Tactical Status.

A Model with this Special Rule may be removed from play without giving any Victory Points to the opponent. In the Effects Sub-Phase of the End Phase of any Turn in which the Controlling Player is the Active Player, they may activate this Special Rule (not possible if the Model is Locked in Combat): make a Cool Check for it, with +1 per enemy Unit within 12", +1 per Tactical Status (other than Routed) it is subject to, and -2 if it is subject to the Routed Tactical Status. If the Check is passed, the Model is immediately removed from play without counting as a Casualty; if it is failed, nothing happens and it may try again in a later Turn.

A Model with this Special Rule may benefit from the Dispersion Advanced Reaction: the Reactive Player may declare it each time a Model with the Dispersal Field Special Rule is the Target of a Shooting Attack, the declaration being made after Step 3 of the Shooting Attack, once the Weapons to be used have been declared (Cost: 1 Reaction Allotment, paid on declaration; Target: the Reacting Unit is the Unit suffering the Shooting Attack, the Attacking Unit is the one making the Shooting Attack that triggered this Reaction). Once the Dispersion Reaction has been declared, the Active Player must resolve all remaining steps of the Shooting Attack Procedure as normal up to the start of Step 5. In that Step 5, the Controlling Player of the Reacting Unit may choose to reduce the Damage of all Hits in one Fire Group to 1. If they choose not to reduce the Damage of the Hits in the selected Fire Group, the Shooting Attack continues as normal, but the Reactive Player may make the same choice again for each subsequent Fire Group in that Shooting Attack. Once the Reactive Player has chosen to reduce the Damage of a single Fire Group, they cannot affect any subsequent Fire Group, and the Shooting Attack is resolved as normal.
A Model with this Special Rule may re-roll a failed Focus Roll in a Challenge, once per Challenge.

A Model with this Special Rule may have a Charge declared for it in the same Turn in which it made a Rush Move, but if the Charge Roll for that Charge fails, it immediately gains the Stunned and Pinned Tactical Statuses. Une fois qu’on connaît le vainqueur du d: Once the winner of the challenge (or the lack of one) is known, the players must return to step 1 and choose a new combat in which to declare a challenge — or, if there are no more eligible combats, end the Challenge Sub-phase and begin the Fight Sub-phase.
Une fois qu’un joueur a choisi une postu: Once a player has chosen a gambit, they apply its bonuses or limitations before the opposing player chooses theirs. Une fois qu’une posture a été choisie, a: Once a gambit has been chosen, no other model in the challenge may choose the same gambit in the same Face-Off Step (if the challenge lasts several rounds, the choices made in one step do not restrict later steps).

Une fois que l’unité cible a fini son dé: Once the Target Unit has finished its move, the Reactive Player may move each model in the Reacting Unit up to a number of inches equal to its base Initiative characteristic, straight towards the Target Unit, without ending within 1 inch of any enemy model that is not part of the Target Unit.
Une fois que les joueurs ont fait leur j: Once the players have made their Focus Rolls and added all modifiers, their totals are compared: the player with the highest total takes the <strong >Challenge Advantage</strong >, and attacks first in the Strike Step, gaining a +1 attack bonus for that Strike Step only (if the challenge lasts over several Strike Steps, this bonus does not carry over). In the event of a tie, both players must re-roll their Focus Roll until one of them has a higher total than their opponent.
Une fois tous les groupes de tirs résolu: Once all Fire Groups have been resolved, units that have suffered heavily test their morale.
Une fois tout le monde placé : <strong>t: Once everyone is placed: Cool test. If failed, the unit gains the Pinned status.
Une fois un round de combat entièrement: Once a round of combat has been fully resolved, determine what happens to both sides in 4 steps.
Une force d’assaut se heurte à une contr: An assault force runs into a determined counter-attack by the defenders: the vanguards of both sides meet in a titanic clash of armour.
Une grande partie de la faune indigène d: Much of the native fauna of Fenris consists of massive and savage predatory creatures. Since Leman Russ took command of his Legion, others have sought to emulate the Wolf King and his own beasts, Freki and Geri, by raising bestial companions of their own. Bonding with such creatures is considered a mark of favour among the sons of Fenris, and those who achieve this feat often rise in rank. On the battlefield, they form a bloodthirsty but loyal pack around their master. Many who have thought to challenge a son of Fenris have ended their days caught in the rending jaws of one of these terrifying creatures.
Une icône avec le blason Emperor’s Child: An icon with the Emperor's Children emblem appears on your home screen.
Une incursion démoniaque de grande ample: A large-scale daemonic incursion requires a significant breach in the veil that separates reality from the Warp, but even the smallest tears are enough to give a handful of lesser Daemons a foothold in reality. Such hordes are often led by a herald of the Ruinstorm, a Daemon seemingly devoted to weakening the barrier between the realms. These heralds display a discipline unusual among their kind, manipulating weak minds and targeting the defenceless to ensure that enough blood is shed to draw other Daemons across the veil.
Une marche lente, obstinée et meurtrière: A slow, stubborn and deadly march through ruins already doomed, where hope survives only long enough to draw one last rescue.
Une mission d’attrition et de progressio: A mission of attrition and advance under pressure, ideal for a dense, dark urban table saturated with ruins in the heart of the Decalian district.
Une mission de duel d’élite et de désint: A mission of elite duels and gradual moral disintegration, where the centre of the table becomes at once trophy, trap and scene of carnage.
Une mission de raid industriel et de con: An industrial raid and counter-intervention mission, ideal for a technical, cold and fragmented table, where each platform becomes a tactical tipping point.
Une mission de siège frontal, idéale pou: A frontal siege mission, ideal for staging massive ramparts, deadly firing lanes and the collision of two utterly opposed doctrines of war.
Une option <strong>rare et avancée</stro: A rare and advanced option, reserved for infantry normally unable to harm a Titan. A unit (Infantry or Paragon only, Movement greater than 0) engaged in combat exclusively against a Titan may, in the Assault Phase, give up all its normal attacks to try to climb the Titan and sabotage one of its profiles.
Une poussée sur un large front, en quatr: A push on a broad front, across four bands of terrain of increasing value.
